hits.text: After him arose Jair, the Gileadite; and he judged Israel twenty-two years.
hits.scopeNotes: No Scripture change proposed; identity may differ across Hebrew Bible and Gospel Jairus.

hits.text: He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkey colts, and they had thirty cities, which are called Havvoth Jair to this day, which are in the land of Gilead.
hits.scopeNotes: No Scripture change proposed; identity may differ across Hebrew Bible and Gospel Jairus.

hits.text: Jair died, and was buried in Kamon.
hits.scopeNotes: No Scripture change proposed; identity may differ across Hebrew Bible and Gospel Jairus.

hits.text: Ben Geber, in Ramoth Gilead (to him [pertained] the towns of Jair the son of Menashe, which are in Gilead; [even] to him [pertained] the region of Argob, which is in Bashan, sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars);
hits.scopeNotes: No Scripture change proposed; identity may differ across Hebrew Bible and Gospel Jairus.

hits.text: Their border was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the towns of Jair, which are in Bashan, sixty cities:

hits.text: There was a certain Jew in the citadel of Susa, whose name was Mordekhai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite,

hits.text: Jair the son of Menashe went and took the towns of it, and called them Havvoth Jair.
